start_here: Say to your AI: "Record a voice take for every line my plans in plans/ have a voice read, using request.json." It runs the voice step and tells you how many lines were new.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads plan files and writes only voice takes (a .wav beside a .txt) in the folder you name.
instructions: 1. Clone the Workshop checkout and install numpy, soundfile, pillow, blake3 (and mlx-audio for the Kokoro speaker).
2. Write request.json with pieces (which segment kind is a voiced_line), plans {folder} and voice {folder, say: [{argv}]} where the last command writes the take at {fill: out}.
3. Say "Voice the lines of my plans"; the AI runs python3 tools/assemble-a-plan-into-a-cut/do-work/assemble.py voice-lines --request request.json.
4. Read lines, had and made; play a made take before it goes into a cut. Run it again: nothing is made twice.

worked_examples.title: One voiced line is made once and then found
worked_examples.ask: Record a voice take of every line my plans have a voice read.
worked_examples.given: From test_1_voice_lines_makes_each_missing_take_once in tools/assemble-a-plan-into-a-cut/test/test_assemble.py, run here on its made-up world with its stand-in speaker: one voiced line, 'What is the made-up question?', and an empty voice folder.
worked_examples.hands_back: First run printed {"result": {"lines": 1, "had": 0, "made": [{"text": "What is the made-up question?", "take": "<voice folder>/7c1d0ce3eb9a8cc8.wav"}]}}, with 7c1d0ce3eb9a8cc8.txt beside it holding the exact words (the name is the first 16 characters of the BLAKE3 of the words). The second run printed {"result": {"lines": 1, "had": 1, "made": []}}.
